hypothesis: Screening-only top candidate: a multi-scale roughness/Hurst-exponent break in detrended elevation may mark degraded fault scarps or damage-zone geomorphology. This was previously proposed in the S18 review; it is not a new project-level hypothesis, is not an assigned lane, and was not tested.
mechanism: Fault-zone fracturing and scarp erosion can produce a cross-strike change in surface-texture scaling where a single-cell slope threshold is weak. This is a geomorphic fault-expression hypothesis, not direct evidence of a geothermal vent.
named_non_fault_mimic: A lithologic boundary with different erodibility; alluvial-fan or playa margins are additional confounders.
